newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND EXAMINES SINKING OF LEROS STRENGTH.
newsitem.headline: POLAND EXAMINES SINKING OF LEROS STRENGTH.

text.p: A Polish deputy minister and prosecutors on Monday began examining the sinking of the Greek ship Leros Strenght in which 20 Polish seaman died last weekend, PAP news agency said.
Piotr Nowakowski, deputy minister of Transport and Maritime Economy, is checking the ship's documents, the seaman's papers of the crew and port authority reports, PAP said.
The Gdansk prosecutor's office meanwhile is examining Poland's competence in the case.

"We must examine our competence in this matter and determine all the circumstances of the disaster. We cannot rule out that someone failed to do their duty," PAP reported Jacek Spyt, a prosecutor's spokesman and saying. He did not elaborate.
The prosecutor's office has 30 days to decide whether to launch an official inquiry into the shipwreck, the agency said.

"The wreck is lying at a depth of 260 metres (yards), too deep for skindivers. The cost of using television cameras would be so great that I doubt whether the Greek ship-owner would agree to cover it," Marek Pielechaty, an expert from Gdynia's Maritime Academy, told PAP.
The ship, a 22,000-tonne bulk carrier went down in a storm off the coast of Norway last Saturday after developing a hole in its bow.
Contrary to initial fears that the families of the victims would be left penniless, the Gdynia Maritime Agency said crew members had been properly insured.
The seamen had been insured with the Liverpool & London mutual insurance club, PAP reported Kazimierz Zalewski,a Gdynia Maritime Agency official, as saying.
Leros Management, the ship's owner, had signed a contract with the Maritime Agency guaranteeing a minimum of $30,000 in damages the families of crew members who died in an accident, Zalewski said.
